owner_questions.question: Only two products are Glättungsstyler (smoothing_styler) in both lanes, and the German market search found just four candidates. Do you accept fewer than five for this one subtype, or should it be merged into a neighbour for v1.0?
examples: KMS Thermashape 2-in-1 Spray: both lanes smoothing_styler (committed).
Color Wow Dream Coat: both lanes smoothing_styler, held until the Leave-in addendum.
Elnett Stylingspray 3 Tage Glatt is ruled smoothing_styler (PH1-14) but has no directions in the packet, so both lanes stop at the evidence gate (P3-4).
options: (a) Lock with a written exception: smoothing_styler stays a subtype with < 5 products (2 now, 3 once the Elnett directions are captured).
(b) Merge smoothing_styler into blowdry_lotion (sleek blow-dry products) or shine_finish for v1.0.
(c) Keep the criterion and wait for the market.
owner_questions.recommendation: (a), and capture the Elnett directions now. Five is not reachable from this cohort even if every open item went the Styling way (see smoothing_styler section).

owner_questions.question: When we only know a product's name from a shop listing (not from the pack or the brand's German page), may that name still decide what the product is — e.g. „Hitzeschutzspray" ⇒ heat protectant, „Haarserum"/„Haaröl" ⇒ Oil?
examples: syoss Hitzeschutzspray Keratin: name only from dm; the only pack line is „2x Frizz-Kontrolle". Lane B: heat protectant (name). Lane A: ignores the name ⇒ anti-frizz product ⇒ unresolved Leave-in border ⇒ review.
Elvital Öl Magique, John Frieda Frizz Ease Haarserum, Garnier Sleek & Stay Haarserum: both lanes say Oil, but lane A only via the owner registry because the „Öl/Serum" name is C3.
owner_questions.recommendation: Yes, for the product-type noun of the shop title when no pack or brand-page name exists (a product's name is identity, not a marketing claim); retailer-only extra words still never count (R2-H1). Also capture the pack names for these five products (29 names are C3 today).

owner_questions.question: The name says one job, but the only pack line joins that job with care. Does the name win?
examples: taft Texturspray Aloe Boost: name „Texturspray" (texture); pack line „Textur und Pflege für mühelose Undone Looks". Lane A: name wins ⇒ Styling texture_spray. Lane B: „Textur und Pflege" is texture + care ⇒ mixed ⇒ manual review — and the standard itself uses this very line as its example of a mixed promise.
owner_questions.recommendation: Yes, the name wins (same logic as your Balea Wax Stick ruling R2-H3: the name decides, later lines are extras). That also lifts texture_spray to 5 agreed products. Delete the Taft example from the mixed list.

owner_questions.question: A smoothing cream with a hold polymer sitting behind a rich conditioning base: Leave-in (like NEQI Ultimate) or hand review (like Wella Flowing Form)?
examples: KMS Thermashape Straightening Creme: Isoamyl Laurate r2 and Triheptanoin r3 (emollients), then VP/VA r5 (hold polymer); „glatte Styles, die bis zur nächsten Haarwäsche halten". Lane A: Leave-in. Lane B: review.
Precedents: NEQI Ultimate (one supporting fixative on a conditioning film ⇒ Leave-in, T15) vs Wella Flowing Form (PVP r2 leads ⇒ review, PH2-1).
owner_questions.recommendation: Leave-in when the hold polymer ranks after the conditioning base (a supporting fixative); review only when it leads (Flowing Form). KMS Creme ⇒ Leave-in. It does not help smoothing_styler coverage either way.
